extracted.intended_audience: publishers, librarians, authors, booksellers, YALSA members, and nominators for the Michael L. Printz Award
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for which books are eligible for nomination and selection for the Michael L. Printz Award, including format, publication date, age-range designation, nomination deadlines, and committee composition. Intended to guide nominators and committee members in submitting and evaluating YA literature for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary excellence in young adult literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Michael L. Printz Award is an award for a book that exemplifies literary excellence in young adult literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is selected annually by an award committee; the committee may also name up to four honor books. This is the primary qualitative standard for choosing the winning title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible formats and creators
rubrics_metrics.description: The award-winning book can be fiction, non-fiction, poetry or an anthology, and can be a work of joint authorship or editorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed formats are eligible; edited volumes and jointly authored works are explicitly permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The books must be published between January 1 and December 31 of the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to the previous calendar year of publication (i.e., only works published within that full calendar year are eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher designation / age-range requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be designated by their publisher as being either a young adult book or one published for the age range that YALSA defines as young adult, i.e. ages 12 through 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on publisher designation or clear intended audience within YALSA's defined 12–18 age range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for both committee and field nominations will be December 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both nominations originating from the selection committee and from the broader field must meet this December 1 deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award may name honor books
rubrics_metrics.description: The award committee can also name as many as four honor books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to selecting a single winner, the committee has discretion to recognize up to four additional titles as honor books for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee composition and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection committee for the award consists of nine YALSA members appointed by the vice-president/president-elect for a one-year term. Beginning in 2002, four members of the committee will be elected by the membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee membership is nine people serving one-year terms; appointment and (partially, from 2002 onward) election procedures are specified for how committee members are chosen.
